learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the basic notions of the following topics: operational amplifiers; output stages of power amplifiers; negative feedback; oscillators; active analog filters; mixers; phase-locked loop (PLL).
Ability to apply knowledge through 'paper and pencil' analysis of simple circuits including operational amplifiers, diodes, transistors.
Ability to perform simulations of medium-complexity circuits including operational amplifiers, diodes, transistors using appropriate circuit simulation software.

Ability to build and test/characterize devices and prototypes in the laboratory (both on breadboards and on printed circuit boards with solderable components) including operational amplifiers, transistors, and diodes.
Ability to critically analyze the result of a characterization measurement of a device or circuit, also by referring to the expected value.
Ability to logically present technical demonstrations on characteristics and properties of devices and specific circuit configurations.
Ability to independently find technical documentation on electronic devices and circuits.

syllabus_topics: Input resistance of a feedback operational amplifier
Output resistance of a feedback operational amplifier
Measurement of current on a load
Frequency response of the open-loop operational amplifier
Frequency response of the closed-loop operational amplifier
Common mode of a CMOS differential stage
Differential mode of a CMOS differential stage
The JFET and BiCMOS operational amplifier
Calculation of beta for the four configurations
Example of BJT amplifier with voltage-voltage feedback
Single BJT amplifier in CC configuration
The oscillation problem of feedback amplifiers
Average power dissipated by a resistive load
CD/CC output stage with source/emitter resistor
CD/CC output stage biased with current generator
Class AB BJT amplifier with Vbe multiplier
Recall on the Fourier series of a square wave
Distortion for a piecewise linear function
Example of using the compression point, HP2 and HP3
VCA with potentiometer in the feedback network
Architecture of a wireless transmission and reception system
teaching_methods: Use of CAD software for electronic circuit design
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as V = ((LAB) + 2(ORA))/3. An insufficient grade is given for serious conceptual errors, fragmented or no understanding, inability to apply knowledge, serious gaps, and lack of autonomy. A minimum of 18 is required for passing. Grades range from 18 to 30 e Lode, with specific criteria for each band. The 'Lode' (cum laude) is awarded for brilliant and original work.
